title.analysis: Rich people pretending poor plus 'not what you think' invites a reversal of stealth-wealth stereotype. No dollar endpoint or instruction; apparent motives rather than steps. Similar plain appearances serve opposite motives: an audience for opting out versus camouflage. Historical and luxury-object analogies widen the critique. Visibility risks lead into a gifted coat that triggers replacement purchases; noticing the chain stops it, while keeping one useful upgrade. A falsely self-made caption finally exposes inherited wealth and invisible labor. The ending returns to Dax’s $340 and limited agency rather than instant success. Named crime anecdotes are unverified. The stored ending is complete; audio and actual footage are unreviewed.
